rules.rule: The skill is discoverable and its description says when to use it
The first output line announces the skill invocation

assertions.value: ▶ Skill invoked: ArchUnit Test — write ArchUnit tests enforcing hexagonal architecture rules in the composition root

rules.rule: The four required inputs are named: target module (default bootstrap), base package, rule sources, rules requested
No file is written while a required input is missing; missing inputs are asked in one batched question

assertions.value: Do not write any file while a required input is missing

rules.rule: ArchUnit is declared as archunit-junit5 with test scope in the target module's POM

assertions.value: only in the target module's POM

rules.rule: The ArchUnit version is managed in the parent POM dependencyManagement
ArchUnit is never added to any module other than the target module, even in test scope

assertions.value: Never add ArchUnit to any other module, even in `test` scope
Adding ArchUnit to any module other than the target module

rules.rule: Tests live in <target-module>/src/test/java/<base-package-path>/architecture/
There is exactly one test class per rule family, with the six named families

assertions.value: one test class per rule family

rules.rule: Rule families state their constraints: onion/layered architecture, domain isolation, adapter dependencies, ports as interfaces, cycles, coding conventions

assertions.value: Spring, Jakarta Persistence / Hibernate, Jackson, Kafka, JDBC
inbound adapters call inbound ports only

rules.rule: Every rule is an @ArchTest field in an @AnalyzeClasses class
Test classes are excluded from analysis with ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
One rule enforces one architectural constraint and carries an explicit .because(...) reason
Every package, port, and layer comes from the rule sources; nothing is invented and gaps are asked

assertions.value: If a source is missing or ambiguous, ask

rules.rule: failOnEmptyShould is kept; a rule is never made to pass on an empty package

assertions.value: never made to pass on an empty package

rules.rule: Temporary exceptions are explicit and narrow (ignoreDependency or FreezingArchRule) with a comment referencing the iteration or ticket

assertions.value: referencing the iteration or ticket ID

rules.rule: Every exception is reported to the caller so it can be tracked and removed

assertions.value: report every exception to the caller

rules.rule: No ArchUnit test is disabled or emptied and no rule is weakened to pass without explicit user approval

assertions.value: weakening a rule to make it pass, without explicit user approval

rules.rule: Rules are written test-first, before the code they constrain is migrated, and RED or GREEN is reported honestly

assertions.value: **before** the code it constrains is migrated
report its RED or GREEN result honestly

rules.rule: The ArchUnit tests are run without Docker and results are reported as actually observed
The report contains the rule catalogue (rule, target, reason, source document, result, exceptions), the files changed, and the results

assertions.value: rule, target, reason, source document, result, exceptions

rules.rule: Deciding the architecture, migrating production code, and deciding when tests are created stay out of scope

assertions.value: Deciding the architecture, layers, packages, or ports
Migrating or refactoring production code to satisfy a rule

rules.rule: A request with missing inputs is answered with one batched question and no file is written
A request to disable a failing ArchUnit test or relax it onto an empty package is declined without user approval
